- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price dips.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use 14-day moving average as a smoothing anchor for final forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, -0.00, 0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast to sentiment’s dominant direction over 3–5 periods.
